Controlling my thoughts? No, nobody is putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are completely my own. Though corporate certainly tries to dictate every single thing we do, if that's what you mean. They send down these planograms—you know, the visual maps for where the product goes on the shelves—and they expect us to follow them like robots.

If the fire marshal walked in, I'd be the one getting the citation, not Mark. The delivery guys know better, too, but they're always rushing because they get paid per stop. 

So... yeah, no one is controlling my mind. They can't even control the backroom inventory properly, let alone my brain.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Less sleep? No, I sleep fine. I usually get my seven hours, unless I'm closing the store and have to open the next morning, which is a scheduling nightmare. They call it a "clopening" shift, and it should be illegal. You leave at 11 PM and have to be back at 6 AM to let the vendors in. 

And speaking of vendors, the guy who delivers our greeting cards—I don't know his name, tall guy, always chewing gum—he came in yesterday and just completely messed up the Mother's Day display. I had spent two hours making sure all the "To a Special Aunt" cards were separated from the "To a Wonderful Grandmother" cards, because people get very upset if they buy the wrong one. Last year, a customer came in screaming because she accidentally bought a "Sympathy on the Loss of Your Pet" card for her sister's wedding. I mean, read the card before you buy it, right? But no, it's always our fault. 

So this vendor just shoves the new stock wherever it fits. I told him, "You can't just put the musical cards next to the blank ones, they have different price points!" The registers won't scan them right, and then the cashier has to do a price override, and if they do too many overrides, the system flags it for loss prevention. And loss prevention is already breathing down my neck because our shrink was up 2% last quarter. Shrink! Half of it is just cashiers forgetting to scan the bottom-of-the-basket items like cases of water. 

But anyway, yeah, I sleep normal. When I actually get to go home and sleep, that is.

The sorting machines don't just magically put the foreclosure documents in the middle of a stack of grocery circulars. \n\nSo, yeah, when that stuff happens, it throws me off a bit because I have to document everything. But otherwise? I'm functioning perfectly fine. Better than most of the people I work with, honestly.\n\nDoctor: During this period, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling rested?\n\nPatient: Less sleep? No, I sleep fine. I usually get my seven hours, unless I'm closing the store and have to open the next morning, which is a scheduling nightmare. They call it a \"clopening\" shift, and it should be illegal. You leave at 11 PM and have to be back at 6 AM to let the vendors in. \n\nAnd speaking of vendors, the guy who delivers our greeting cards—I don't know his name, tall guy, always chewing gum—he came in yesterday and just completely messed up the Mother's Day display. I had spent two hours making sure all the \"To a Special Aunt\" cards were separated from the \"To a Wonderful Grandmother\" cards, because people get very upset if they buy the wrong one. Last year, a customer came in screaming because she accidentally bought a \"Sympathy on the Loss of Your Pet\" card for her sister's wedding. I mean, read the card before you buy it, right? But no, it's always our fault. \n\nSo this vendor just shoves the new stock wherever it fits. I told him, \"You can't just put the musical cards next to the blank ones, they have different price points!\" The registers won't scan them right, and then the cashier has to do a price override, and if they do too many overrides, the system flags it for loss prevention. And loss prevention is already breathing down my neck because our shrink was up 2% last quarter. Shrink! Half of it is just cashiers forgetting to scan the bottom-of-the-basket items like cases of water. \n\nBut anyway, yeah, I sleep normal. When I actually get to go home and sleep, that is.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when these beliefs about the bank and people at work happened even when your mood felt otherwise normal?\n\nPatient: My mood? Yeah, my mood is totally fine. I mean, I'm just a normal person going about my day when all this stuff happens. Like, I'll be perfectly fine, having my morning coffee—I always get the hazelnut blend, not the French roast, because the French roast gives me heartburn. I told the girl at the cafe down the street, \"Just one pump of hazelnut,\" but she always puts in two, and it makes it way too sweet. You'd think it wouldn't be that hard to follow a simple instruction, right? It's like nobody listens anymore. \n\nJust like at the store. I'll be having a great day, totally normal mood, and then I'll find out someone left the freezer door cracked in the back room. Do you know how fast a pallet of frozen pizzas thaws? Fast. And then we have to damage it all out. The paperwork for damaged goods is ridiculous. You have to scan every single barcode, and the scanner gun we have in the back is held together with duct tape. Literally, silver duct tape wrapped around the handle because someone dropped it on the concrete floor two months ago. I put in a requisition for a new one, but corporate rejected it. They said we haven't met our equipment depreciation threshold yet. What does that even mean? It's broken! \n\nSo, yeah, my mood is fine. I'm not depressed or anything when I notice what they're doing with the mail or how people are acting. I'm just paying attention. Someone has to pay attention, especially when corporate won't even buy us a new scanner gun.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that people on TV, the radio, or the internet were sending special messages meant specifically for you?\n\nPatient: Messages on the TV or the internet? No, I haven't seen anything like that. I mean, I watch TV to unwind, mostly those home renovation shows. Have you seen the one where they flip the houses in Texas? The couple that does it, they always want to knock down every single wall to make an \"open concept.\" I don't get it. Where do you put your furniture if you don't have any walls? And the smells! If you're cooking fish in the kitchen, the whole house is going to smell like fish if there are no walls to stop it. \n\nI was telling my sister that the other day. She called me while I was watching it, complaining about her HOA again. Her homeowners association is ridiculous. They sent her a warning letter because her trash cans were visible from the street for two hours after the garbage truck came. Two hours! She was at work, how was she supposed to bring them in? I told her she should just paint them the same color as her house so they blend in. Her house is this awful shade of beige, though. Builder's beige, they call it. \n\nBut anyway, no, the TV is just regular shows. And the internet is mostly just me checking the store's inventory system from home, which I'm not supposed to do off the clock, but if I don't check it, the morning shift will completely mess up the restocking. Last week they put all the seasonal allergy medicine in the clearance bin. It's April! That's prime allergy season! I had to pull it all back out and re-tag everything. So, yeah, no special messages or anything, just the usual headache.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?\n\nPatient: No, definitely not. People can't hear what I'm thinking. If they could, I probably would have been fired from my job a long time ago with the things I think about my district manager. He came in last Tuesday for a walkthrough, wearing these ridiculous loafers without socks. Who wears leather loafers without socks? It just seems so unhygienic. And he was pointing out every little thing, like the dust on the top shelf of the greeting card aisle. \n\nI mean, nobody looks up there! Unless you're seven feet tall, you can't even see the top shelf. But he made me get the ladder out right then and there. The rolling ladder we have is so wobbly, I always feel like I'm going to break my neck. The right wheel gets stuck because a piece of a plastic hanger got jammed in the caster like three years ago and nobody can figure out how to pry it out. I've tried needle-nose pliers, tweezers, even a screwdriver. It just drags across the linoleum and leaves these black scuff marks that the night crew complains about. \n\nThe head of the night crew, Gary, he leaves me these passive-aggressive Post-it notes on my desk about the scuff marks. He writes them in red Sharpie. Who uses red Sharpie for a casual note? It feels like I'm being graded. I should just buy him a pack of blue pens and leave them on his cart. But anyway, no, my thoughts are private. Brenda is always clocking in exactly four minutes late because she insists on parking under the one oak tree in the plaza lot so her car doesn't get hot. But the tree is at the very back of the lot! Mine was starting to crack from the sun anyway, which is annoying because I just paid off the car last year. It's a Honda, so it'll run forever, but you still want the interior to look nice, you know? \n\nBut no, no weird forces or impossible devices. Just the broken cameras and Kevin.\n\nDoctor: Have you found it harder to motivate yourself to start everyday tasks, like showering, cooking, or doing chores?\n\nPatient: Motivate myself? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still get up and shower and go to work every day. I have to, right? If I don't open the store, nobody will. I'm the one with the master keys. Well, me and the district manager, but he's obviously not going to come down at 6:30 in the morning to unlock the doors. He's probably still asleep in his fancy house, you know? \n\nI actually saw a house like his on Zillow the other day. I wasn't looking to buy, obviously, retail doesn't pay that well. I just like to look at the pictures sometimes. This one had a huge kitchen island. It was marble, I think. Or maybe quartz? People are really into quartz right now because it doesn't stain like marble does. My sister's friend got marble countertops and spilled red wine on them the first week. You can't get red wine out of porous stone. I told her she should have gone with butcher block, it's so much warmer looking anyway. \n\nButcher block does require maintenance, though. You have to oil it, like, once a month with food-grade mineral oil. I bought a bottle of it once for my cutting board, but I always forget to use it. It's sitting under the sink right next to the dish soap. I buy the bulk size dish soap from Costco and refill the smaller bottle by the sink. It saves so much money, honestly. \n\nBut yeah, chores and stuff? I get them done. I mean, the laundry isn't going to wash itself, right?\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the bank and people at work are able to do things that would be impossible in real life to make this happen?\n\nPatient: Impossible in real life? Like magic or something? No, of course not. The bank is just a bank. They just use regular computers and paperwork, you know? Though, honestly, their paperwork is a mess. I had to go in there last month to update my address because I moved to that new apartment complex off Route 9. \n\nThe teller, she had these really long acrylic nails.
